![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/5ff3d7cda0ee3fbc807a4bacbd3a739d72d83d0020271936ba77e6afbc89b83f.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{5}{8},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{5}{8}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{5}{8} & =\frac{3x-2}{4x} \\ 5(4x) & =8(3x-2) \\ 20x & =24x-16 \\ -4x & =-16 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x-2=3(4)-2=10, \\ AC & =4x=4(4)=16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16\cdot 10 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$
